title: TraXion: Rethinking Pre-training Frameworks for Mobility and Beyond
abstract: arXiv:2605.06906v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Human mobility differs from text and from generic time series in three structural ways: visits are tuple-valued events whose meaning depends on the joint distribution over location, time, and activity; users carry persistent signatures across trajectories; and visits are not independent across users, since co-location at shared places is a primary signal. Existing pre-training recipes for mobility import objectives from language modeling, treating trajectories as sentences and visits as tokens, an analogy that fails against each of the three properties above. These properties define a broader class, multi-entity spatiotemporal event streams (MESES), spanning enterprise authentication logs, electronic health records, and other event-stream domains where entities share infrastructure, schedules, or contexts. translated_title: TraXion：重新思考移动性及更广泛领域的预训练框架
translated_abstract: 人类移动性与文本以及通用时间序列在三个结构性方面存在差异：访问（visits）是元组值事件，其含义取决于位置、时间和活动的联合分布；用户在轨迹间携带持久的特征签名；访问在用户之间并非相互独立，因为在共享地点的共同出现（co-location）是一个重要信号。现有的移动性预训练方法从语言建模中借用目标函数，将轨迹视为句子、访问视为词元，但这种类比在面对上述三个属性时均会失效。这些属性定义了一个更广泛的类别——多实体时空事件流（MESES），涵盖企业认证日志、电子健康记录以及其他实体共享基础设施、日程或情境的事件流领域。我们将这些属性精确表述为任何MESES预训练框架都应满足的三个公理，并引入了TraXion框架。
tldr: 该论文提出TraXion预训练框架，将移动数据所具有的元组值事件、用户持久签名和跨用户关联三个结构特性形式化为多实体时空事件流（MESES）应满足的公理，从而克服了将轨迹当作句子、访问当作词元的语言建模式预训练方法的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TraXion, a pre-training framework that formalizes three structural properties of mobility data—tuple-valued events, persistent user signatures, and cross-user dependencies—as axioms for multi-entity spatiotemporal event streams (MESES), overcoming the limitations of language-modeling-style pre-training that treats trajectories as sentences and visits as tokens.
